name: Beijing Jiaotong University
overview:
Additional Programme Specifics

  • Students with a Chinese passport are not allowed to apply to this university


Beijing Jiaotong University

Beijing Jiaotong University (BJTU) is one of the most important universities in China. Its history dates back to the Qing Dynasty in 1896.

Located in downtown Beijing in the Haidian district, which is recognized as the "Cradle of Higher Education" in China, BJTU covers an area of 78 hectares and is made up of two campuses, East and West. The two campuses are very well laid out, and offer many facilities and a beautiful environment. Just north of the university is Zhongguancun, the computer village known as the "Silicon Valley" of China.

BJTU is one of the first universities to have been selected for the national programs “National 211 Project” and “985 Strength Discipline Innovation Platform.” It plays an important role in the development of the Chinese railway industry, having contributed massively at each stage of the sector’s development.

Epitech students will study at the School of Software Engineering (SSE). Created in 2001, it employs practice-based learning, and in 2009 received first prize for the best computer training program among the 36 software engineering schools of China.
administrative:
1. Application dossier

You will be working directly with the partner university regarding your application.

Your host university may ask for the following documents:

  • Create your account and apply online: https://bjtu.17gz.org/
  • Guarantor in China: you can fill this section with BJTU's contact information (mentionned in the factsheet you'll receive). For 2025/2026:
  • Li Tao (Sophie) Email: taoli1@bjtu.edu.cn – Phone no.: +86 010 5168 7122 – WeChat: +86 13802181723


I- Basic Info

  • Personal Photo : Please upload your recent full-faced passport size photo taken within the last 3 months (jpg, jpeg)
  • Family Name and Given Name : You need to fill exactly as your passport.
  • Chinese name : Optional
  • Birth Date : Fill exactly as your passport
  • Employer or Institution Affiliated: You should fill the employer or Institution Affiliated at present. If you don’t have any employer or Institution, please fill None.
  • Occupation : You should fill your occupation at present.
  • Passport No. and Passport Expiry Date : Fill extactly as your passport
  • Other basic info


II- Eduaction and Employment

  • Educational Background: Undergraduate applicant should fill the education background from high school
  • Employment Background: Fill in your working experiences as complete as possible. If you have, please upload in section "Other Documents upon Request" your latest work certificate


III- Upload documents

  • Personal Information Page of Passport
  • Certificate of Enrollment (Original and translation in Chinese/English)
  • Transcript (Original and translation in Chinese/English
  • Foreigner physical examination form (within 6 months) Print and have the Physical Examination Record document filled out at the hospital. Make an appointment very early because the deadlines for exams and results are long! Remember to bring the original to BJTU to present on arrival. The sample form can be downloaded from: http://cie.bjtu.edu.cn/contentType/7.htm
  • Letter of Recommendation
  • Financial support statement: all applicants include CSC or other scholarships should provide it
  • No proof of criminal record (original and translation in Chinese/English)
  • Others : If you have participated in any activities or won any prizes, you can upload the relevant certificates here


To be given to Epitech campus administration:

  • Addendum to the contract
  • EPITECH re-registration dossier

This information is subject to change by the partner university. They will provide you with the most current information upon your acceptance.


You must apply online

  1. Online Services can be accessed via : Online Service Platform for International Students
  2. Select 'register' to start your application form as a new user
  3. Registration agreements : Please click on 'Accept' to accept all the conditions mentioned below
  4. Online Registration Checklist : contains a checklist of the registration details that need to be entered before you confirm your registration. Fill in the form by entering all information needed. Once you have filled in the form, click 'register' to go to the next step.
  5. Confirmation email : Once information are filled in, you will be shown a page asking you to check your email to activate the account.
  6. Activate your account : After signing in to your email you will see the link to activate your account within 72h. By clicking to the link you will be redirected to the page saying you have successfully activated your account. (Please use within the 72h, past taht period, the link will no longer be valid)
  7. Choose your program then click next
  8. Select your type : choose the type you want to apply to and click next
  9. Apply Section : students must first search for the major they want to do and select the field corresponding to that major.
  10. Application query : Fill the application form by clicking on edit. Complete each step in the application query, save then move on to the next step. Once your application is submitted you cannot go back to change any information


2. Acceptance letter

Once you've completed your online application, you will receive your acceptance letter.

Please be patient, this might take a few weeks.


3. Application for a study visa and the Chinese residence permit

You must take the necessary steps in obtaining a study visa type X1 upon receipt of the letter of admission and the form JW202 (sent to you by email). Please check this site for more information. Price: between 110 and 130€ (2025). You can also entrust the file to an agency by clicking here.


The X1 visa is an entry visa valid for 3 months from the date of entry into China. After your arrival, you must obtain a Chinese residence permit within 30 days of entering China.


The host university will assist you with visa conversion procedures, medical examinations, and obtaining the resident permit.

Related costs are the responsibility of the students (see estimated budget at the bottom of the page).


Please note:

  • For the latest information regarding visa application, you should contact your nearest Embassy/Consulate of China.
  • After you arrive in the Chinese mainland, the X visa for single entry cannot allow you to exit and re-enter the Chinese mainland. You must stay in the Chinese mainland until the Residence Permit is granted.


4.Insurance and Health

You will be asked to undergo medical examinations after arriving in Beijing.

The results must be presented to the Beijing Bureau of Exit and Entry Administration of the Ministry of Public Security when you apply for a residence permit.


The costs of these exams will be borne by the student (see “Estimated Budget”).


According to the regulations made by Chinese Ministry of Education, all the international students in China are required to purchase comprehensive insurance and the valid period should cover the duration of their studies. You may subscribe to the insurance on the registration day at BJTU if it's not required for your visa application. The steps to subscribe to BJTU insurance must only be carried out once in China.


In order to be fully covered for medical care, we recommend that you take out international insurance as well. It is imperative that you take out insurance that will cover you for your medical and hospital expenses, repatriation and accompanied by civil liability. International insurance must cover the entire period of your studies in the country. Insurance costs are the responsibility of each student. To take out international insurance, the market is quite open. Please click here for more information.


For more information, you can consult the country's health file at: https://www.pasteur.fr/fr/centre-medical/preparer-son-voyage/chine

Note: It is advisable to register on the French registry established outside of France and to report to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs via the Ariane platform: https://pastel.diplomatie.gouv.fr/fildariane/dyn/public/login.html 


5.Prepare your arrival

For advice to travelers issued by the Ministry of Europe and Foreign Affairs on China, click here.


Campus life

Student's feedback (2024-2025): "Life there was good, there was a lot of free time to go to the gym, swim, play basketball. Things are cheap so you can do a lot of things. There are a zoo and an aquarium next to the school; as well as a lot of restaurants, multiple coffee shops and supermarkets on campus. There are 8 different cafeterias, even some with halal food. There are also multiple student associations (hard to get in though) dedicated to archery, volleyball, Chinese lion dance..."
accomodation:
On-campus accommodation (more information here)

BJTU Student Apartments is the preferred option for our international students. There are four buildings are available for international students. On-campus dormitories (four people in a room) are equipped with public kitchen, laundry room, private bathroom, TV set, phone, WIFI, air-conditioner, single bed (including bedding), bookshelves and wardrobe.

Students must take care of their rooms (cleaning products are not provided by the university) and respect the curfew.

Students who voluntarily leave their university accommodations during their studies are not allowed to sublet their room to a third party.

The rent for university accommodation will not be reimbursed.

The accommodation cost of campus residence is about CNY16,200-21,600/year/person (about 2500€ - for reference only and subject to final adjustment of prices each year).

Exchange students can pay by day: CNY40-60/day/person.

A deposit will be required before you have access to the room (1000 yuan per person).


Off-campus accommodation

Students can also rent apartments outside the campus by themselves.

Student's feedback (2024-2025): "It’s not as cheap as you might think. I stayed in the university dormitories for the first semester, then moved to an apartment nearby. I paid around €1,100 per month, which is quite expensive because the area around BJTU (Haidian District) is costly. If you’re on a budget, staying in the dorms or sharing a flat with other students is a better option."


Finding accommodation via reputable rental agencies

Due to its close proximity to Tsinghua University, many students living off campus choose to live in apartment blocks located in the Wudaokou and Liudaokou areas.


Below are the main rental agencies in China. Before your arrival, you can first access their websites to learn of their accommodation options. Then once in China, you can go to their neighborhood shopfronts to request to view properties.


Ziroom is a popular choice for foreigners renting in Beijing. They have an easy-to-use app that also has an English interface for searching for accommodation. Once securing accommodation via Ziroom, on the app you can find the details of your accommodation, including the contract and details on your payments made. Included in the contract is a service fee, which includes regular cleaning of the public spaces of the apartment, and also easy servicing for repairs. You will also be advised to add your agent on WeChat for ease of contact.

courses:
Credits

All students must complete 32 local credits (not counting the internship) which is equivalent to 60 ECTS at Epitech for this international year.


Academic calendar

September - mid June


Department and courses

Classes are taught in English. Our students will follow the course in the same class with other international students.

You will find the list of courses here: curriculum master program.

You will also have Chinese classes (six hours a week).


Important notes

  • Presence in class is compulsory, under penalty of loss of visa and repatriation to France at the student's expense (impact on credits).
  • The courses are most likely more academic than at EPITECH.
  • The course list is given for information only. It can change from year to year.
  • If a course is not available when you arrive on site, EPITECH cannot be held responsible for it.
  • Any Tech 4 abroad involves an EIP! Take advantage of the free slots you will have to advance it.
cost:
Financial Overview (4th year Epitech)

  • You must pay the tuition fees for the 4th year of EPITECH, as well as the re-registration fees and related fees.
  • EPITECH covers the tuition fees.
  • The tuition supplement payable by you is indicated at the top of this page (if applicable).
  • Other costs at your expense include: travel, accommodation on site, insurance, and everyday expenses (books, food, transport, etc.).


Other Expenses

  • Roundtrip flights: from 1000€ depending on the company & the dates
  • Insurance from BJTU: about 100€
  • Additional insurance: 300-600€ for additional insurance contract depending on the coverage
  • Visa: between 110-130€
  • Medical examinations in China: about 100€
  • Accommodation deposit: 1000 yuan (about 120€)
  • Chinese residence permit: 500 yuan (60€), etc.


Estimated monthly budget

The local currency is the Yuan (RMB or CNY). 1 € = 8.26 RMB (rate as of October 2025).

Please check the Numbeo website to compare the cost of living between your city of origin and your city of exchange. Please note that everyone's budget will be different according to one's lifestyle.


We advise you to plan a monthly budget of minimum 300€ for your expenses (can go up to 700€ depending on your lifestyle according to former students), rent excluded.


Student's feedback (2024-2025): "When traveling, expenses could rise to around €1,200–1,300, especially for destinations like Zhangjiajie or Guilin. Food is generally cheaper than in France, but in Beijing, prices are higher than in most other Chinese cities. You can eat for under €5 per day if you mostly eat at the school cafeteria, but you’ll probably want to explore more local restaurants too, they’re inexpensive and delicious."


"If we don't take the accommodation in account, I was around 500-600€ a month, but you can easily stay between 270-400€ (but try to have fun, you won't have many opportunities such as this one). You can also easily get higher than that depending on your needs."


  • Housing:
  • about 2000€/year if you live on-campus
  • 300€-1000€/month if you live off-campus (but please note that the city is huge and that living near campus is costly. Living on-campus is recommended.)
  • Food: 100-150€
  • 1€ a meal to 15€ (good meal in a restaurant)
  • Transportation
  • Metro: Around 5 yuan (~€0.60)
  • Bus: 1 to 2 yuan
  • Phone, internet: 12€/month for internet in the studios / 6€ phone
  • If you’re with Free Mobile, their €20/month plan includes some roaming data in China, which can be very helpful for the first few days. Otherwise, you can easily buy a local eSIM or a China Unicom SIM card at the airport for short-term use.
  • Leisure;100-200€
  • For nightlife, if you are European, entry and drinks are usually free
  • For monuments and cultural sites, most have an entry fee
  • In 80% of cases, you get student discounts with your student card

These prices are indicative and may vary.


Additional Information (specifics, advice, useful links, etc.)

  • Get a good VPN. Internet restrictions in China can be tricky, so a reliable VPN is essential. Students have mentioned the following three, which work consistently well: MullvadVPN, Let’sVPN, and ChamVPN. Make sure to install and test them before arriving in China, as VPN websites are usually blocked there.
  • The Trip.com app is extremely useful, you can book everything from flights and trains to hotels and activities directly from it. It supports English, accepts international payment cards, and usually offers better prices than foreign apps.
  • Open a Chinese bank account. This is extremely important. Many popular Chinese platforms such as Taobao (the main online shopping website) don’t always accept foreign cards, and WeChat Pay or Alipay charge small fees when using international cards. Having a local bank account allows you to transfer money easily from your foreign account, convert euros to yuan, and avoid extra charges. It’s also much more convenient in daily life: without a Chinese card, you can’t send money to friends through WeChat, which makes it complicated to split bills or reimburse someone after a restaurant or a trip. Opening an account at ICBC, Bank of China, or China Construction Bank is usually straightforward, as long as you bring your passport and student card.
  • Take slow trains to travel around China; for long trips, take a sleeping train to make the journey feel quicker. China has excellent and affordable high-speed trains, making it easy to visit places like Shanghai, Xi’An, Hangzhou, Chengdu, or Harbin.
  • Download WeChat and Alipay, they’re essential for daily life in China (payments, communication, deliveries, etc.). You can link them to an international bank card like Wise or Revolut. Other useful apps include: Taobao (equivalent of Amazon), Tencen map or Gaode map, Meituan, Didi (taxis—don’t take the one at the airport!), Xiao Hong Shu (equivalent of Instagram), Ctrip.
